about: What the viewer's "Fields…" hands to the field page kisi-advanced.html with a segment's cross-section (2D) or a via (3D), and the 3D view's defaults (web/src/field-views.js, web/advanced/fdtd/, docs/reference.md "Field views").

sources.text: A lane is shown at the Nyquist frequency of its interface profile (data/interfaces.json); a net without a profile at 1 GHz, which the page's title says. 2D and 3D alike; the 3D view offers its presets beside it.
Peak values. Single-ended 1 V; a pair 1 V between the conductors (odd mode, ±0.5 V) or 1 V common mode (even mode, +1 V on both). Every view scales with it; the field shapes do not depend on it.
Annealed copper, IEC 60028: 5.8e7 S/m, as kisi's line models.

RMS roughness for the page's gradient model (Grujić, IEEE T-MTT 70(4), 2022) fitted to kisi's Huray presets (kisi_si::rf::Roughness: HVLP r 0.5 µm SR 0.5, standard r 1 µm SR 1) in the loss factor, 1-20 GHz least squares: HVLP 0.27 µm (3 % rms), standard 0.66 µm (9 % rms). Estimates.

kisi's own adaptive mesh, so that the page's quasi-static solve of the same cross-section gives kisi's numbers: the settings of web/solver/backend_forsten.js (the solver's initial grid nx = ny = 10, solve_adaptive with 60 k nodes, one converged pass and the error certificate), with kisi's tolerance FIELD_TOL (web/src/field-cache.js, 1 %) as the page's energy and parameter tolerance (fork patch 0004). The page's own defaults are a 30-cell grid, 5 % parameter tolerance, 20 k nodes and two passes. The full-wave backend takes the same node cap, tolerance and passes.

3D view (kisi-fdtd in the browser): frequency presets and the frequencies chosen first without a hand-over; a board via is cut out with a 1.2 mm keep box (kisi-validate via-case's default), feeds of 2.5 mm and a 1.5 mm margin (shorter than the 3D references' 4 mm / 2.5 mm, fewer cells; the feed is a straight line from the keep box on).

Mesh first chosen for a board via: coarse (0.07 mm) for a single via, standard (0.05 mm) for a pair – 0.07 mm does not resolve the 0.13 mm gap of a typical pair (validation/vias.md, the board vias' quick meshes: |S21| within 0.07–0.20 dB of the reference mesh up to 20 GHz).

Estimates before a run: the simulated time to the stop level a + b/fmax ns (fit of kisi-fdtd runs of the examples; board vias ring longer in their plane cavities), the setup per million cells (WebAssembly; board vias with polygon copper take longer), 75 B per cell and 48 B per field node and frequency (docs/research/fdtd-field-view.md); a warning above 300 MB per worker or 600 MB in all – phones are warned, no limit is enforced.
